def payroll_overtime_count(rows):
    """
    Okay, payroll question for you, and I promise it's a small one. Every
    other Thursday I pull the raw timesheet export out of our payroll
    system before the pay run gets finalized, and it lands in my lap as a
    plain Python list called rows. Each element of rows is a list of
    exactly three values: a name (str), a qty (int), and a unit (int).
    The name is whatever identifier the upstream system stamped on the
    entry — usually an employee name, though sometimes it's a placeholder
    string the exporter drops in when a record looks odd, so don't read
    anything into it. The qty is the hours figure for that entry, and the
    unit is an internal pay-code number that finance uses for bucketing;
    for what we're doing here you can ignore it completely.

    What I actually need is embarrassingly simple. Company policy treats
    a standard workweek as 40 hours, and anything past that is overtime
    that has to get flagged for the supervisors before checks go out. So
    before I forward the file, I want a quick headcount of the overtime
    entries. Count how many rows have qty strictly greater than 40.

    That's genuinely the whole job — no grouping by name, no summing
    hours across entries, no arithmetic with the unit codes. Just hand me
    back that one number so I know how many entries need the supervisor
    flag. Some pay periods it'll be a big pile, some weeks (holiday weeks
    especially) there may not be a single one, but either way all I want
    is the tally so I can drop it into my little pre-run checklist and
    move on with my afternoon.

    Examples:

    >>> payroll_overtime_count([])
    0
    >>> payroll_overtime_count([['error', 41, 3]])
    1
    """
